title: Introduce adaptive payload clamping and proxy writer backpressure for stable toolcall streaming
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: We see periodic regressions in streaming stability for complex tool/function-calling sessions when large prompt contexts or oversized attachments trigger headroom exhaustion in the gateway proxy writer. This manifests as partial fncall handshakes, truncated structured output events, or long tail latency spikes under bursty traffic. Goal: reduce tail errors and keep OpenAI-compat behavior stable while preserving throughput. What this PR does: 1) Adaptive payload clamping: gateway now estimates token-equivalent size per-request and applies a route-configurable clamp that prefers smaller payload routes when the estimate exceeds a route-specific threshold. Clamps are conservative defaults but are overridable per-tenant and by model family to avoid breaking customers. 2) Proxy writer backpressure: the streaming proxy gains a soft-write-window with hysteresis and an explicit retry-after signal propagated to the runtime. The proxy now buffers up to N chunks (configurable) and applies exponential backoff on fncall/writer stalls instead of immediate aborts. 3) Fncall handshake resilience: we add a lightweight preflight validation for structured function call payloads to catch malformed tool schemas before the streaming path. When a handshake fails, the gateway attempts a single automatic fallback to the compatibility text-stream framing with an audit log entry. 4) Compatibility mapping tweaks: fixes edge cases in openai-compat chunk framing where empty metadata frames could be misinterpreted as terminal events; also ensures idempotency tokens and original-request route metadata are forwarded for tool retry semantics. 5) Observability and feature gates: granular metrics added (gateway.payload_clamp.evicted, proxy.writer.backpressure_enter, fncall.preflight.fail) plus feature flags gated behind runtime rollout. Testing: synthetic load tests in benchmark-lab and canary traffic for 48h on staging; unit and integration tests added. Rollout plan: start with opt-in flag for Dedicated customers, then enable gradually for hosted API after 2 days of healthy canary. Related: ENG-2182 (investigate streaming tail errors), ENG-2210 (toolcall stability spike). Motivation and risk: These changes reduce transient truncation and partial-toolcall incidents at the cost of modest increase in gateway CPU and slightly more buffering memory during bursts; defaults are conservative and can be tuned per-tenant. See release notes for operator-visible knobs.

release_notes: Introduce gateway adaptive payload clamping (route-configurable), proxy writer backpressure with soft-write-window and retry/backoff for streaming toolcalls, fncall preflight validation with automatic text-stream fallback on handshake failures, new observability metrics and feature gates. Impact: reduces partial fncall/truncation incidents; operator knobs for thresholds and buffer sizes are in configs/feature_flags.yaml.
